context: A SaaS billing system migrated EU card charges from Stripe to Adyen on 2026-04-01. The ledger table is payments(provider, provider_reference, event_type, order_id, amount_cents, currency, booked_at_utc, ledger_day, idempotency_key). The nightly reconciliation compares ledger_day totals against provider exports grouped by UTC settlement date. Since the migration, internal net revenue is 0.37% higher than provider exports. The mismatch is concentrated in EUR refunds booked between 23:00 and 01:00 UTC; captures match within 0.02%. There are no job failures. A sample duplicate log says: duplicate idempotency_key=PSP_89344:2026-04-02 existing_event_type=capture skipped_event_type=refund provider=adyen order_id=ord_77. The new ingestion code computes ledger_day = formatDate(booked_at_utc in merchant.timezone) and idempotency_key = provider_reference + ':' + ledger_day. Stripe capture and refund references were distinct; Adyen refund webhooks reuse the original capture pspReference and add eventCode=REFUND plus a unique eventId. The replay job reuses the same dedupe path and currently ignores eventId. Finance wants a backfill but is worried about double-booking old Stripe refunds.
task: Diagnose the most likely root cause of the reconciliation drift, propose the smallest safe fix, and outline verification plus rollout steps.
title: Billing Reconciliation Drift After Provider Migration
